questions.prompt: Which of these is an open question?

options.text: “How’s the setup working now that you’re at six locations?”
“Is the owner the one who decides?”

questions.reveal: It can’t be answered with yes or no, and the prospect picks the direction.

questions.prompt: The owner of a three-location yoga studio says “We’re pretty set.” Best next line?

options.text: “If you could change one thing about your setup, what would it be?”

questions.reveal: “Pretty set” is a surface answer. A what-would-you-change question gets under it without arguing.

questions.prompt: Which rung of the question ladder puts a cost on the problem?
questions.reveal: Impact questions turn “annoying” into hours, money or members lost.

questions.prompt: Which is a leading question?

options.text: “What does your front desk spend most of its day on?”
“Wouldn’t it be easier if clients could book themselves?”

questions.reveal: It’s a pitch with a question mark. The prospect can only agree or push back.

questions.prompt: Two questions in, the prospect has talked for about 15 seconds total. What’s the likeliest cause?

options.text: Your questions are closed, so the answers are short

questions.reveal: Short answers usually mean yes/no questions. Open it up before you judge the prospect.

questions.prompt: On a good discovery call, who talks more?

options.text: The prospect, with each question coming from what they just said

questions.reveal: If you’re talking more, you’re pitching, not discovering.

questions.prompt: A Pilates group’s director says “Reporting across the studios is a bit of a mess.” Best next question?

options.text: “What does ‘a mess’ look like week to week?”

questions.reveal: Pull on their exact words. The detail under “a mess” is what the AE needs.

questions.prompt: “Members can’t see waitlist spots, so they email us and we add them by hand.” What is this?
questions.reveal: It’s specific, it costs staff time, and it came from them.

questions.prompt: A prospect says “It’s fine. The app’s a bit clunky.” Which word do you pull on?
questions.reveal: “Fine” is the polite surface. “Clunky” is the crack.

questions.prompt: The prospect names their first real pain. What do you usually do next?

options.text: Pitch the feature that fixes it
Ask for the meeting right away
Ask one more question to see what it costs them

questions.reveal: One more layer turns a complaint into a reason to meet.

questions.prompt: What is an impact question for?

options.text: Putting a cost on the problem so it matters

questions.reveal: Cost is what makes a busy owner give up 30 minutes for a demo.

questions.prompt: A wellness practice’s operations manager says “Our providers spend a lot of time on the phone rescheduling.” Best impact question?

options.text: “Roughly how many hours a week does that take across the team?”

questions.reveal: It asks for a number they can feel, without suggesting the answer.

questions.prompt: Which of these is checked before the call, not on it?

options.text: Who else is involved in the decision

questions.reveal: Pre-vetting covers the website and location, so the call is spent on things you can’t see.

questions.prompt: What size does an account need to qualify?
questions.reveal: Either one is enough.

questions.prompt: What’s the most natural way to confirm you’re talking to a decision-maker?

options.text: “Who else would want to be in the room when you look at options?”

questions.reveal: It confirms the title and maps the decision without putting them on the spot.

questions.prompt: When is the best moment to ask about contract timing?

options.text: When they talk about switching or what they’d change

questions.reveal: Tied to something they said, it reads as interest, not a checklist.

questions.prompt: Midway through, the prospect mentions they run on Mariana Tek. What do you do?

options.text: Thank them, close the call politely and don’t book it
Book it anyway and let the AE sort it out

questions.reveal: Mariana Tek, Gymmaster and ClubReady accounts don’t qualify. Booking one wastes the AE’s slot.

questions.prompt: Their website shows three locations. Best way to cover it?

options.text: “I saw you’ve got three locations. Is that right?”

questions.reveal: Confirm what you already know. Asking it cold tells them you didn’t look.

questions.prompt: What should you do right before you ask for the meeting?

options.text: Play back their words and check you got it right

questions.reveal: The playback makes the ask about their problem, not your calendar.

questions.prompt: The prospect named manual reporting and double-bookings. Best playback?

options.text: “So it’s the manual reporting and the double-bookings. Did I get that right?”

questions.reveal: Their words, then a check. They say yes to the summary before they say yes to the meeting.

questions.prompt: Mid-discovery, the prospect asks “How much is it?” Best move?

options.text: Ignore it and change the subject
Say it depends on their setup, the AE will walk through it, then ask a question back

questions.reveal: Answer honestly, keep pricing with the AE, and keep the conversation moving.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a discovery killer?

options.text: Pitching the first pain they mention

questions.reveal: Pitching early ends discovery before you’ve found the real reason to meet.

questions.prompt: A studio manager has described a real pain and confirmed it’s costing the team hours. What now?

options.text: Play it back and ask for the meeting

questions.reveal: Pain named and confirmed is the signal you’ve earned the ask.

questions.prompt: After naming a clear pain, the prospect says “Just send me some info.” Best response?

options.text: Ask them to sign up today
Ask for the meeting three more times
Tie it back to the pain they named and ask for a short call with the AE

questions.reveal: Info gets skimmed. Their own problem is the reason the meeting is worth it.

questions.prompt: What goes in “Why specifically are they taking the call?”
questions.reveal: The AE opens the demo with this line.

questions.prompt: Which pain-point note helps the AE most?

options.text: “Pulls numbers from six locations into a spreadsheet every Monday, about 3 hours”

questions.reveal: Specific and quantified. The AE can build the demo around it.

questions.prompt: What belongs in the tech stack field?

options.text: Leave it blank unless they bring it up
Every tool they mentioned: booking, payments, marketing, website

questions.reveal: The AE needs the full picture to plan the switch.

questions.prompt: The prospect mentions they’re opening a fourth location in the spring. Where does it go?

options.text: General notes, because it shapes the demo

questions.reveal: Growth plans change what the AE shows.

questions.prompt: Why write the note right after the call?

options.text: Details fade fast and the AE needs their exact words
The system locks after an hour

questions.reveal: Exact words are the first thing to go.

questions.prompt: A note reads “Owner. Good call. Interested.” What’s missing?

options.text: The pain, why they took the call, and the tech stack

questions.reveal: The AE would walk in blind.
